newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Drazek says EU still studying biotech corn.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Drazek says EU still studying biotech corn.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department senior trade adviser Paul Drazek said the European Union was still studying whether to approve genetically-altered corn and indicated a decision would not come in the near term.
"The Europeans are still studying the issue," Drazek said in a telephone interview with USDA Radio from Brussels Tuesday after talks with top European Commission officials.

"They were not in a position to say that they (biotech corn) would be approved in the near term, meaning within the next few weeks but on the other hand they also were not prepared to say that they would not be approved," he said.
The corn, developed by Ciba-Geigy, produces a naturally occurring chemical to repel the European corn borer, a damaging pest.
Washington has been pressing Brussels to speed up approval before the U.S. crop is harvested.

On genetically engineered soybeans, which were approved for marketing earlier this year by the EU, Drazek said that despite criticism from European consumer groups there did not seem to be a groundswell of opposition to the beans.
